title: Staged launch traffic slicing playbook (working)
content:
Status: rough working doc for cross-functional teams (product, console, serving-runtime, SRE, solutions-eng) to follow when creating staged launches that rely on traffic segmentation and automated fallback.

Purpose:
- Capture traffic-slicing patterns we use across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Provide a checklist and decision tree for canary vs. A/B, fallback policies, and escalation.
- Surface minimal instrumentation and SLOs needed to run safe staged launches.

Context / motivation:
We repeatedly run into ambiguous ownership and inconsistent signal thresholds when doing partial rollouts for new model versions, console UX changes, or routing policy updates. This leads to either overly cautious launches (slow iteration) or bad rollouts that require painful rollbacks. This playbook attempts to standardize the traffic-slicing surface area and quick decision heuristics that ship teams can follow.

High-level patterns (quick summaries):
- Progressive ramp (canary): start with 0.1% → 1% → 5% → 25% → 100%. Use for ops-sensitive changes (serving runtime, quantization, core model).
- Shadow then compare: mirror 5–20% of traffic to new variant without responding to users, collect quality/latency metrics then decide. Use for model semantic change experiments.
- A/B split: deterministic user-wide allocation (50/50, 10/90): use for UX experiments or personalization where direct comparison is needed.
- Region-specific slices: route only in non-critical regions (e.g., EU-beta) before global rollout.
- Tier-aware slices: route only to non-SLA customers or dev accounts for risky changes.

Minimum instrumentation checklist (must be wired before any staged launch):
- Request-level tracing flag indicating slice id and experiment id.
- Per-slice latency p50/p95, error rate, token-rate counters (1m, 5m windows).
- Quality signals for model changes: rejection rate, hallucination heuristics (if available), eval set regression alerts.
- User impact metrics: % of requests with degraded payloads, client-side error reports (console SDK).
- Alerting: Pager duty action on >X% error or sustained latency degradation >Y for 10m.
- Dashboard: one per rollout with slice breakdown and quick links to logs and traces.

Suggested thresholds (starting defaults — adjust per product):
- Critical error rate (5xx or internal errors): >0.5% at 5m → pause ramp; >1% at 5m → automatic rollback.
- Latency p95 increase: absolute increase >200ms or relative >2x sustained for 5m → pause and investigate.
- Quality regression on golden prompt set: >3% downstream metric drop (e.g., correctness score) → hold and triage.
- User-reported severity: any P1 report within first 30m → consider immediate rollback.

Canary vs. A/B decision flow (simple):
1) Is this change infrastructure/serving/latency sensitive? → Canary.
2) Is this change purely UX/behavioral and needs unbiased comparison? → A/B.
3) Does the new variant need scaled traffic to detect rare regressions? → Use progressive canary with longer dwell.
4) If uncertain, start with shadowing for 24–72h, then choose.

Operational roles and responsibilities (cross-functional):
- Owning PM (launch owner): defines success criteria, golden prompts, business metrics, rollback thresholds.
- Engineering owner (deploy owner): creates routing config, implements feature flags, coordinates infra changes.
- Observability lead (console/telemetry): builds dashboard, wires alerts, ensures traces include slice metadata.
- SRE/Oncall: monitors alerts during ramp windows, owns rollback execution if automation fails.
- Solutions/CS: monitors customer tickets and flags high-risk customers to exclude.

Runbook snippets (playable steps):
- Pre-launch (48–72h): set up dashboards, register rollout with product-launch calendar, announce to SRE and CS, create rollback PR and smoke-test plan, run shadow for 24h.
- Day-of launch: start at agreed UTC time, enable 0.1% slice, monitor 30m. If stable, move to next bucket. Keep manual approval barrier at 5% and 25% (product + eng).
- Automatic rollback conditions: if any of the thresholds above are tripped and oncall confirms, feature flag turned off for slice and traffic rebalanced. Postmortem required if rollback happened.

Fallback strategies (ordered preference):
1) Instant feature-flag off (per-slice): fastest, least global impact.
2) Route to fallback model variant (older quantized or smaller model) if degradation is quality-specific but still acceptable.
3) Region-level rollback: if issue isolated to infra region.
4) Full global rollback: last resort.

Testing and simulation guidance:
- Load test with traffic patterns approximating real token distributions at 5x expected load before hitting 25% ramp.
- Run adversarial prompts and golden set against new model variant on staging.
- Chaos test routing fallback beforehand in staging (simulate partial failures).

Template: rollout metadata (copy into a new rollout doc)
- rollout_name: short title
- owner: name + pager
- impacted_components: console/api/routing/model etc.
- variant_ids: list of model or route ids
- slice_strategy: percentage/rules/region/tier
- start_time_utc:
- checkpoints: list (0.1%, 1%, 5%, 25%, 100%)
- metrics_to_watch: latency p95, error rate, biz-metric-x, golden-eval
- rollback_triggers: free-text thresholds
- runbook_link: URL

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define per-product default thresholds (we currently use the same numbers for everything; some products are more latency sensitive).
- Automate cross-slice rollbacks when global capacity is affected.
- Add SDK headers for sampling slice id for downstream observability.

Short-term action items (owners assigned):
- Maya: finalize default dashboard template (due 2026-03-07).
- Diego: add slice-id header to request tracing (PR in progress).
- Evelyn: schedule shadow-run playbook with solutions-eng for the next model onboarding (by 2026-03-15).
- Arjun: propose sane product-specific thresholds for hosted-api and dedicated (WIP).

Notes to self / fragments:
- Consider gating canary progress by both absolute token count and time (e.g., min 10k tokens AND 30m dwell).
- We should publish a one-pager for customers explaining what staged launches mean and opt-out controls (private/dedicated customers often demand control).

Appendix (links / references):
- Staged deployment signal runbook (internal) — see linked_artifacts.
- Existing rollout examples: PROJ-1172 (model quantization rollout), PROJ-1298 (console search revamp).

This doc is intentionally iterative. Add notes here as you run rollouts; if you find missing signals or better thresholds, add a short changelog bullet at the top.
